### 2. parameter-object-callsite-semantic-argument-binding

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Both cited anchors resolve live in `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ParameterObjectService.cs` (1171 lines). The call-site rewriter builds its parameter-slot map purely lexically in `BuildRewrittenArgumentList` at lines 1044-1066: `var semanticArgs = new ArgumentSyntax?[method.Parameters.Length]` then `if (arg.NameColon is null) { if (positionalIndex < semanticArgs.Length) semanticArgs[positionalIndex] = arg; positionalIndex++; }`. Four concrete defects follow. (1) **In-position named arguments** (C# 7.2+): `positionalIndex` is not advanced when a `NameColon` argument occupies its own declared position, so a subsequent positional argument overwrites an already-filled earlier slot — `M(a: 1, 2, 3)` maps `2` onto slot 0. (2) **Reduced-extension receivers**: `method.Parameters` for an extension method includes the `this` parameter at index 0, but a reduced invocation `receiver.M(x)` supplies no syntactic argument for it, shifting every slot by one. `EnforceParameterShapeRefusals` (lines 549-553) only refuses `IsThis` when the receiver is itself *grouped*, so the ungrouped-receiver case reaches the rewriter unguarded. (3) **Ungrouped trailing `params`**: `EnforceParameterShapeRefusals` (lines 544-548) only refuses a `params` parameter that is *grouped*; a legal ungrouped variadic tail hits the `positionalIndex < semanticArgs.Length` guard at line 1051 and every argument past the first is silently dropped from `outerArgs`, emitting a call that loses arguments. (4) **Evaluation order**: the outer argument list is re-emitted in *parameter* order by the loop at lines 1103-1118, so a source call that supplies named arguments out of declaration order is rewritten with its expressions reordered — a silent change of left-to-right evaluation order for side-effecting argument expressions. The identical lexical slot bug is duplicated in `CollectProvidedParameterNames` (lines 676-698, `positionalIndex++` at 690), which feeds the `CollectDefaultValueWarningsAsync` refusal gate at lines 641-674 — so the guard that is supposed to catch omitted grouped arguments mis-attributes names on the same call shapes and can pass a call it should refuse. `CollectCallerSpansAsync` (lines 582-605) collects raw `SymbolFinder.FindCallersAsync` source spans with no invocation-shape classification, so method-group and non-invocation references reach `RewriteCallSitesAsync` (line 971 `FirstAncestorOrSelf<InvocationExpressionSyntax>()`) where they are silently skipped rather than refused — a preview token is stored claiming an atomic rewrite that did not cover every reference. |
| Approach | Single-file change to `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ParameterObjectService.cs`. (a) Add a private helper `TryBuildSemanticArgumentSlots(SemanticModel model, InvocationExpressionSyntax invocation, IMethodSymbol method, out ArgumentSyntax?[] slots, out IReadOnlyList<ArgumentSyntax> extraVariadicArgs, out string? refusalReason)` that reads `model.GetOperation(invocation)` as `IInvocationOperation` and derives every argument-to-parameter association from `IArgumentOperation.Parameter` / `ArgumentKind` instead of a lexical index — this is the same operation-API pattern already used in this file by `ClassifySemanticVariableRequiredUse` (lines 458-486, `semanticModel.GetOperation(reference, ct)` + `is IInvocationOperation invocation && ReferenceEquals(invocation.Instance, operation)`), so mirror it. The helper resolves reduced extensions via `IInvocationOperation.TargetMethod` / `.Instance` and collects `ArgumentKind.ParamArray` children so every trailing variadic argument is retained, not just the first. (b) Make the helper the single refusal point: return a refusal reason for any invocation whose operation is null, whose `TargetMethod.ReducedFrom`/`OriginalDefinition` does not match the target, whose argument set cannot be mapped completely, or whose source left-to-right expression order differs from the parameter order the rewriter must emit (refuse rather than reorder — preserving observable evaluation order beats a best-effort rewrite). (c) Thread a `SemanticModel` into `RewriteCallSitesAsync` (lines 940-1003) — it already holds `baselineDocument`/`doc`, so add `await doc.GetSemanticModelAsync(ct)` next to the existing `GetSyntaxRootAsync` call at line 977, matching the pattern already at line 792 — and pass it to `BuildRewrittenArgumentList` (line 988), replacing the lexical block at lines 1044-1066 with the helper's slots and appending `extraVariadicArgs` to `outerArgs` after the parameter loop at lines 1103-1118. (d) Rewrite `CollectProvidedParameterNames` (lines 676-698) to consume the same helper so the default-value refusal gate and the rewriter agree by construction. (e) In `CollectCallerSpansAsync` (lines 582-605), classify each collected source location: non-invocation and method-group references become a refusal (thrown before the preview token is stored at line 126), not a silent skip. All refusals must throw before `_previewStore.Store` on line 126, satisfying the "refuse before storing a preview token" acceptance. |
| Scope | Production files: 1 — `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ParameterObjectService.cs`. Test files added/modified: 1 — `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ParameterObjectPreviewTests.cs` (extended with new methods). No files deleted. No Rule 3 exemption claimed or needed (1 ≤ 4). Rule 4 satisfied (1 ≤ 3). Changelog fragment `changelog.d/parameter-object-callsite-semantic-argument-binding.md` is the repo's fragment convention and is not counted in the production budget. |

### 3. parameter-object-value-type-mutation-semantics

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Anchors verified live. `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ParameterObjectService.cs:358` `EnforceGroupedParametersAreReadOnlyAsync` walks every `IdentifierNameSyntax` in the target method body that binds to a grouped parameter and refuses when `ClassifyVariableRequiredUse` (line 412) returns a kind. That classifier only recognises whole-variable writes and aliases: simple/compound assignment where the reference IS the assignment target (`IsDirectAssignmentTarget`, line 517, compares `target.Span == reference.Span`), pre/post increment, address-of, `__makeref`, `ref` expressions, `ref`/`out`/`in` arguments (line 448), and the semantic `ref` extension receiver / `ref this` cases (`ClassifySemanticVariableRequiredUse`, line 458). Two value-type mutation shapes fall straight through and are silently mis-rewritten: (a) a mutating instance member call on a non-readonly struct parameter — `value.Mutate();` binds `value` as an `IInvocationOperation.Instance` with `RefKind.None`, so line 478 returns null unless the target is a `ref` extension; (b) a nested field/property write through the parameter — `value.Field = 1;` has an assignment `Left` of `MemberAccessExpressionSyntax`, whose span never equals the reference span, so `IsDirectAssignmentTarget` returns false. In both cases the preview proceeds and the rewrite turns `value` into a positional-record property read, so the mutation lands on a temporary struct copy: `value.Mutate(); return value.State;` compiles cleanly and silently returns the pre-mutation state — exactly the Evidence in the detail file. The same shapes on a REFERENCE-type parameter (member mutation, array element write) are semantically equivalent through the DTO property and must keep working, so the guard has to be value-type-conditioned, not blanket. |
| Approach | Single production file: `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ParameterObjectService.cs`. (1) Thread the bound `IParameterSymbol` into the classifier: change `ClassifyVariableRequiredUse` (line 412) to take the parameter symbol — its only caller is line 392, which already has it in hand. (2) Add a private helper `ClassifyValueTypeMutation(reference, parameter, semanticModel, ct)` invoked from `ClassifyVariableRequiredUse` after `ClassifySemanticVariableRequiredUse` returns null, and only when `parameter.Type.IsValueType` and the type is not a readonly struct (`INamedTypeSymbol.IsReadOnly`) — reference-type parameters short-circuit to the existing behavior, satisfying the do-not-over-refuse acceptance. (3) Inside the helper detect two shapes, mirroring the operation-based style already established in `ClassifySemanticVariableRequiredUse` plus `UnwrapTransparentOperation` (line 488) for conversions/parens: (a) `IInvocationOperation` whose `Instance` is the parameter reference and whose `TargetMethod.IsReadOnly` is false and whose containing type is a struct, returning the kind string `"mutable value-type member call"`; the same check on `IPropertyReferenceOperation` used as an assignment target covers mutating setters; (b) a syntactic receiver-chain walk for assignment / compound assignment / increment-decrement whose `Left` (or operand) roots at this reference through `MemberAccessExpressionSyntax` or `ElementAccessExpressionSyntax` segments that are ALL value-typed — returning `"value-type member assignment"`. The chain walk stops (returns null, no refusal) the moment a segment's type is a reference type, which is what keeps `refParam.Field = 1` and array-element writes eligible. (4) No change to the refusal plumbing: `EnforceGroupedParametersAreReadOnlyAsync` already formats `'<param>' at <file>:<line> (<kind>)` and throws before any preview token is stored (`_previewStore.Store` is line 126, far downstream), so the new kinds automatically satisfy the "refuse before preview, naming parameter and use location" acceptance with zero extra code. Deliberately NOT implementing the alternative acceptance branch (explicit local plus write-back lowering) — see Risks. |
| Scope | Production files: 1 — `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ParameterObjectService.cs`. Test files added/modified: 1 — `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ParameterObjectPreviewTests.cs` (extended with new methods). Changelog fragment `changelog.d/parameter-object-value-type-mutation-semantics.md` per the repo's fragment convention (not counted in the file budget). No Rule 3 exemption claimed or needed — 1 of 4 production files, 1 of 3 test files. No public surface change, so no `ServerSurfaceCatalog` / `README.md` / DI addenda touches. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 35000 |
| Risks | Over-refusal on unannotated structs is the main behavioral risk: a struct instance method that does not mutate but is not marked `readonly` (common in older third-party and BCL types) will now be classified as a mutation and refuse the preview. That is a deliberate safe-fail — a refusal with an actionable message beats the current silent state corruption — but it narrows the tool's accepted input, so the refusal text must tell the operator to omit the affected parameter. Second risk: the receiver-chain walk must not treat a value-type segment reached THROUGH a reference-type segment as a mutation (`param.RefField.ValueField = 1` is fine, since the copy happens at the reference boundary and the write still lands on the shared object); getting the stop condition backwards causes exactly the over-refusal above. ### 4. parameter-object-generic-dto-type-validity

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Anchors verified live. `BuildDtoSource` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ParameterObjectService.cs:743-758`) emits `grouped[i].Type.ToDisplayString()` straight into a NON-generic `sealed record` declaration with zero validation of the parameter type. Three concrete defects: (a) **generic scope** — a parameter typed by a method type parameter (`method.TypeParameters`) or a containing-type type parameter produces `public sealed record Foo(T Value);` in a new top-level file, where `T` is unbound (CS0246); nothing in the pipeline inspects type parameters, and the only type-parameter awareness in the file is the unrelated name-collision check at `:243`. (b) **accessibility** — `ResolveDtoProject` (`:557-580`) picks the record's visibility purely from `method.ContainingType.DeclaredAccessibility` / cross-project (`:566`, `:578`); a `public` record whose positional member types are `internal`/`private`-nested yields inconsistent-accessibility errors, and a cross-project DTO is *forced* public at `:578`, maximizing the exposure. (c) **cross-project availability** — `EnforceCrossProjectReferences` (`:607-639`) only checks that the method/caller projects reference the *DTO project*; it never checks the reverse direction, so a DTO placed in project B referencing a type declared only in project A (or in an assembly A references but B does not) emits an unresolvable type name. All three fail AFTER the refusal gates and reach `_previewStore.Store` at `:126`, so a malformed preview token is persisted and handed back to the caller. Existing refusal gates (`EnforceParameterShapeRefusals` `:535-555`, `EnforceGroupedParametersAreReadOnlyAsync` `:358`, `CollectDefaultValueWarningsAsync` `:641`) establish the throw-before-store pattern this fix extends. |
| Approach | Single production file: `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ParameterObjectService.cs`. Three checks, each throwing `ArgumentException` in the message style of `EnforceParameterShapeRefusals` (`:539-553`) — prefix `"parameter_object_preview refuses: "`, name the offending parameter AND its type: (1) **Generic scope** — recursively walk each `IParameterSymbol.Type` (element/type-argument/pointed-at types) collecting any `ITypeParameterSymbol`; a hit refuses, naming the parameter, the type-parameter, and its declaring symbol. Refusal (not propagation) is the chosen arm of the acceptance's "propagate ... or refuse" — the record emitted by `BuildDtoSource` is structurally non-generic and threading type parameters + constraints through the record declaration, the rewritten signature (`RewriteMethodDeclaration:864`) and every `new Foo(...)` callsite (`BuildRewrittenArgumentList:1093`) is a materially larger initiative than this `size: S` row. (2) **Accessibility** — compute each parameter type's effective accessibility (min over containing types + the type itself, walking type arguments) and refuse when it is less accessible than the record visibility chosen at `:566`/`:578`; also refuse when `dtoCompilation.IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, dtoCompilation.Assembly)` is false.
